xhci98 1.1.1.0-usos3-w9x - MODIFIED version of xhci98 1.1.1.0 (GPL-2.0-only)

This is NOT an upstream release. It was modified by the Universal Service OS
(USOS) project on 2026-09-29 to 2026-10-05 (GPL-2.0 section 2a notice). Upstream:
https://github.com/yeokm1/xhci98 (Yeo Kheng Meng), tag v1.1.1.0 = commit
7d0dd9d440e9716a87e0882f905bf8e99fa443ac. Report problems with this build to
USOS, not upstream.

Corresponding source: the upstream tag tarball
(tools/vendor/xhci98/1.1.1.0-src/, pinned in ../1.1.1.0/SOURCES.txt) plus
patches/0001-usos1-*.patch, patches/0002-usos2-*.patch, patches/0003-usos3-*.patch and
patches/0004-usos3-w9x-*.patch, applied in order
with "git apply" in the unpacked xhci98-1.1.1.0 directory; build.cmd does both and
builds with WDK 7.1 (toolchain.txt). Every changed spot in the source carries
a "MODIFIED (USOS 1.1.1.0-usos1)", "(... usos2)", "(... usos3)" or
"(... usos3-w9x)" comment; src/xhci_usos.c is new.

Why: on an ASRock X470 + Ryzen 7 5700X (Server 2003 x86 SP2 under CSMWrap)
xhci98 1.1.1.0 started the Promontory chipset xHCI (1022:43D0) but never the
CPU xHCI (1022:149C). The firmware leaves 149C with decoding and bus
mastering off at ExitBootServices (no BootConfig in the registry); NT 5.x
PCI.SYS assigns the BAR and enables decoding, and xhci98 refuses a controller
whose Bus Master Enable it did not clear itself (init step 3).

Changes:
 1. src/xhci_usos.c XhciUsosPciPrepare, called before the bus-master gate:
    PCI power state D0 (restores the BARs if D3hot->D0 reset them), then
    Memory Space Enable and Bus Master Enable if clear (Linux:
    pci_enable_device + pci_set_master).
 2. src/xhci_init.c: wait for USBSTS.CNR = 0 (up to 10 s) before the first
    USBCMD write; HCRST/CNR timeout 1 s -> 10 s (Linux XHCI_RESET_LONG_USEC);
    USBLEGSUP: if the BIOS does not release within 1 s, clear BIOS_OWNED
    and set OS_OWNED anyway (Linux quirk_usb_handoff_xhci); raw capability
    words and PCI command/PMCSR recorded in the log ring.
 3. src/xhci.h: XHCI_MAX_SCRATCHPAD 64 -> 256 (AMD controllers were never
    measured upstream; the common buffer grows by 768 KiB).
 4. Log file: every start refusal, successful start and stop is appended to
    %SystemRoot%\xhci98.log (C:\WINDOWS\xhci98.log) by a system thread that
    retries for up to 15 minutes until the boot volume is reachable
    (src/xhci_usos.c, src/xhci_dispatch.c, src/xhci_log.c/.h). Switches in
    the device's software key: XhciLogFile (1 on) and XhciLogVerbosity
    (2 = note ring); both default to on when the value is ABSENT (text-mode
    Setup), and the INF writes 1 and 2. Each flush starts with
    "=== xhci98 1.1.1.0-usos2 flush reason=R pci=DDDDVVVV step=S status=X
    tick=T dropped=D ===" (reason 0 stop, 1 start refused, 2 start OK;
    step = XHCI_INIT_STEP_* of src/xhci.h, 22 = done).
 6. usos2 (after the X470 run of usos1, 2026-09-29): 149C was refused at
    XHCI_INIT_STEP_PORT_MAP with XHCI_CAPS_TOO_MANY_PROTOCOLS (its PCI state
    was already fine, command 0x0007, D0). XHCI_MAX_PROTOCOLS 4 -> 16
    (src/xhci.h; the UCHAR index and its 0xFF sentinel, the port-map
    layout assertion, XhciPortMapEqual, the post-reset re-parse and the
    slot-type lookup all follow the constant). Companion pairing tries the
    next USB 2.0 group when the first one took no pair (one capability per
    port). The raw xECP chain (usos.xecp.*, usos.proto.dw2/dw3) and the
    parsed groups (usos.map.group: major<<24|minor<<16|first<<8|count,
    usos.map.group.psi.slot) are logged on the preflight pass, before any
    refusal. 64-byte contexts (CSZ=1, 149C): reviewed, no change needed;
    every context offset is index x ContextSize, the Input Context
    (33 x 64 = 2112 bytes) and Device Context stride (2048) are reserved
    for CSZ=1, builders write 8 DWORDs into a block zeroed at full size.
 5. Version string 1.1.1.0-usos2 (FileVersion/ProductVersion, Comments);
    INF DriverVer 09/29/2026,1.1.1.0 and a MODIFIED header.

 7. usos3 (after the X470 Windows 2000 run of 2026-10-05): under the 2000
    MPS HAL (CSMWrap's MP table has no PCI INTx entries) PCI.SYS gives both
    xHCI functions no interrupt resource, so usbport refused the start
    (Code 10, no xhci98.log). Polling is the default (Parameters\PollMode
    = 0 turns it off; GUI Setup restores SYSTEM from system.sav on every
    restart, so a registry switch did not survive): the driver registers without USB_MINIPORT_FLAGS_INTERRUPT and drops the
    interrupt bit from the start's resource check; USBCMD.INTE/IMAN.IE are
    never enabled and PCI INTx is disabled (command bit 10). A periodic
    kernel timer (4 ms, i.e. every clock tick) asks usbport for a soft
    interrupt (USBPORT_INVALIDATE_CONTROLLER_SOFT_INTERRUPT), which runs the
    normal InterruptDpc path and drains the event ring; if usbport answers
    eight soft interrupts in a row with no InterruptDpc, the timer runs the
    miniport's InterruptDpc body itself. With PollMode = 0 the
    same timer only steps in when the event ring has held events for three
    ticks with no claimed interrupt (a routed but dead line). Counters
    usos.poll.* (ticks, softints, direct, rescues, dpcs) are logged at stop;
    usos.poll.mode at start. src/xhci_usos.c, src/xhci_dispatch.c,
    src/xhci.h, src/xhci_hw.h; version string 1.1.1.0-usos3.

 8. usos3-w9x (2026-10-05, the Windows 98 SE package): installed 98 SE
    under CSMWrap on the X470 has no PS/2 at all, and the USOS keyboard
    bridge (SeaBIOS INT 16h) gives no mouse. Patch 0004 adds the build
    switch XHCI_USOS_W9X (environment XHCI_USOS_W9X=1, src/sources), used by
    build.cmd here:
     - no file sink (upstream measured that asking 98's ntkern for write
       access to a file hangs the boot, design record 08 section 13.0.1);
       the sink functions become empty stubs, so no Zw*/Ps*/Ob* imports;
     - no PollMode registry read (98 has no service key for an NTMPDriver
       miniport): polling is fixed on, for the same reason as usos3 - under
       CSMWrap nothing guarantees a routed PCI INTx line;
     - KeSetTimer re-armed on every tick instead of KeSetTimerEx (not
       exported by 98's ntkern); KeRemoveQueueDpc dropped (98 is
       uniprocessor, the in-DPC counter wait stays);
     - no /GS cookie (its init imports KeTickCount and KeBugCheckEx) and PE
       subsystem version 5.00 like upstream's Windows 2000 DDK build.
    Every remaining kernel import is also imported by a Windows 2000 USB
    driver of the NUSB 3.3 set that runs on 98 SE (KeSetTimer,
    KeInitializeTimer, KeInitializeDpc, KeCancelTimer,
    KeDelayExecutionThread) or by upstream's 98 build. Version string
    1.1.1.0-usos3-w9x.
    release-x86/xhci98.inf: the usos3 INF plus (a) disk 2 = STACK.CAB, the
    cabinet of the user's USB 2.0 stack installer (NUSB), with usbport.sys
    (in [Xhci.CopyW98], flag 16) and usbhub20.sys taken from it, and (b) the
    USB 2.0 root hub USB\ROOT_HUB20 bound to usbhub20.sys through
    *NTKERN/NTMPDriver ([Xhci.RootHub20]). USOS puts the INF, xhci98.sys and
    STACK.CAB into the Windows 98 SE Setup folder, so Setup's device
    detection installs controller, root hub and HID devices without a
    prompt and without the stack's own INF.

Scope: x86 only (WDK 7.1 WNET target with XHCI_USOS_W9X=1), staged by USOS
only for Windows 98 SE installs under CSMWrap. Not tested on Windows Me,
2000 or NT 5.x; use 1.1.1.0-usos2/usos3 there.
